verses.greek: Ἰάκωβος θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ χαίρειν.
verses.literal: James of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ a servant To the twelve tribes the in the Dispersion Greeting.
verses.dgt: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: greetings.

verses.greek: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε, ἀδελφοί μου, ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις,
verses.literal: All joy do esteem it brothers of mine when trials you may fall into various
verses.dgt: Consider it all joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you encounter various trials,

verses.greek: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν·
verses.literal: knowing that the testing of your the faith produces endurance
verses.dgt: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

verses.greek: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.
verses.literal: the And endurance work its perfect should have so that you may be perfect and complete in nothing lacking.
verses.dgt: And let endurance have its complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.

verses.greek: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας, αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος, καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ·
verses.literal: If now any of you lacks wisdom he should ask from the One giving God to all generously and not finding fault and it will be given to him.
verses.dgt: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let that person ask from God, who gives generously to all without reproaching, and it will be given.

verses.greek: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ·
verses.literal: he should ask however in faith nothing doubting The one for doubting he has been likened to a wave of the sea being blown by the wind and being tossed by the wind.
verses.dgt: But let that person ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind.

verses.greek: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου
verses.literal: Not for should suppose the man that that he will receive anything from the Lord
verses.dgt: For that person must not suppose that anything will be received from the Lord,

verses.greek: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος, ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.literal: He is a man double-minded unstable in all the ways of him.
verses.dgt: a double-minded person, unstable in all their ways.

verses.greek: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ,
verses.literal: should boast however the brother the of low degree in the exaltation of him
verses.dgt: Let the lowly brother or sister boast in their high position,

verses.greek: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται.
verses.literal: he who is then rich in the humiliation of him because like a flower of grass he will pass away.
verses.dgt: and the rich in humiliation, because like a flower of grass the rich person will pass away.

verses.greek: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο· οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται.
verses.literal: Has risen for the sun with its burning heat and withered the grass and the flower of it has fallen and the beauty of the appearance of it has perished Thus also the rich man in the midst of the pursuits of him will fade away.
verses.dgt: For the sun rose with scorching heat and dried up the grass, and its flower fell and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich person will fade away in the midst of pursuits.

verses.greek: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς, ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
verses.literal: Blessed is the man who endures trial because approved having been he will receive the crown the of life that He has promised to those loving Him.
verses.dgt: Blessed is the person who endures trial, because having stood the test that person will receive the crown of life, which he promised to those who love him.

verses.greek: μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ θεοῦ πειράζομαι· ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν, πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα.
verses.literal: No one being tempted should say that By God I am being tempted the For God unable to be tempted is by evils tempts now He Himself no one
verses.dgt: Let no one being tempted say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God is untemptable by evil and he himself tempts no one.

verses.greek: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος·
verses.literal: A man however is tempted by the own desire being drawn away and being enticed
verses.dgt: But each person is tempted when being dragged away and enticed by their own desire.

verses.greek: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.
verses.literal: Then the desire having conceived it gives birth to sin the and sin having become fully grown it brings forth death.
verses.dgt: Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.

verses.greek: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.
verses.literal: Not do be misled brothers of mine beloved
verses.dgt: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers and sisters.

verses.greek: Πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν, καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, παρʼ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα.
verses.literal: Every act of giving good and every gift perfect from above is coming down from the Father the of lights with whom not there is variation or of shifting shadow.
verses.dgt: Every good giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow due to turning.

verses.greek: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.
verses.literal: Having willed it He brought forth us by the word of truth for the to be us firstfruits a certain the of His creatures.
verses.dgt: Having willed it, he gave birth to us by the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

verses.greek: Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν,
verses.literal: You should know brothers of mine beloved should be however every man swift unto the to hear slow unto the to speak slow unto anger.
verses.dgt: Know this, my beloved brothers and sisters: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,

verses.greek: ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται.
verses.literal: the anger for of man the righteousness of God not works.
verses.dgt: for human anger does not produce the righteousness of God.

verses.greek: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
verses.literal: Therefore having put aside all filthiness and excess of wickedness in humility do receive the implanted word which is being able to save the souls of you.
verses.dgt: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and abundance of wickedness, receive with gentleness the implanted word that is able to save your souls.

verses.greek: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.
verses.literal: do be however doers of the word and not hearers only deceiving yourselves.
verses.dgt: But become doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.

verses.greek: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ,
verses.literal: because if anyone a hearer of the word is and not a doer this one has been likened to a man looking at the face the natural of him in a mirror
verses.dgt: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, that person is like someone observing the face of their birth in a mirror,

verses.greek: κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.
verses.literal: he has viewed for himself and has gone away and immediately he has forgotten what like he was.
verses.dgt: for that person observed themselves and went away and immediately forgot what they were like.

verses.greek: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.
verses.literal: The one however having looked intently into the law perfect that the of freedom and having continued in it not a hearer forgetful having been but a doer of the work — this one blessed in the work to be done by him will be.
verses.dgt: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and remains in it—not becoming a forgetful hearer but a doer of work—this one will be blessed in the doing.

verses.greek: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.
verses.literal: If anyone seems religious to be not bridling the tongue of him but deceiving the heart of him of this one worthless is the religion.
verses.dgt: If anyone thinks themselves religious while not bridling their tongue but deceiving their heart, that person’s religion is worthless.

verses.greek: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.
verses.literal: Religion pure and undefiled before the God and Father this is to visit orphans and widows in the tribulation of them unstained oneself to keep from the world.
verses.dgt: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself unstained from the world.
